get.description: Answers 204 when the Worker is deployed and serving. Use it for uptime checks; it reads no storage.

post.description: Signs a browser in with the deployment's API token: answers 204 with the sign-in cookie, HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite=Strict, for /api, kept 30 days. The API then accepts it in place of the bearer token. A wrong token answers 401 and sets nothing.
Signs the browser out: answers 204 and removes the sign-in cookie.
The options that make the invited person's passkey on this site, good for 5 minutes. 403 for an invitation that is wrong, used, or older than 7 days.

Joins with the passkey made from joinOptions: the new member, signed in with the sign-in cookie, HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite=Strict, for /api, kept 30 days. The invitation is used up; a passkey that doesn't hold answers 400 and leaves it open.
The options that sign in with any of this site's passkeys, good for 5 minutes: pass them to navigator.credentials.get().
Signs in with a passkey answering signInOptions: the member, signed in with the sign-in cookie for 30 days. 401 for a passkey the deployment doesn't know, or an answer that doesn't hold.

get.description: The member who calls: an owner sees every project; a member, the projects listed.

post.description: The options that make another passkey for the member who calls, on this site, good for 5 minutes: pass them to navigator.credentials.create().
Adds the passkey made from passkeyOptions to the member who calls. 400 when it doesn't hold, such as for options used already.

get.description: The browsers signed in with passkeys, the latest seen first, each with what it is, when and where from it signed in and last called, and whether it is the one asking: an owner sees every member's, a member their own.

delete.description: Signs a browser out: its sign-in stops working at once. An owner signs out any; a member, their own.

get.description: Every member, owners first. Owners only.

post.description: Invites someone to see these projects: a link, <deployment>/invite#<code>, good once for 7 days, which makes their passkey and signs them in. Send it to them yourself. Owners only.

put.description: Sets the projects a member sees. Owners only, and not for an owner.

delete.description: Removes a member: their passkeys, sign-ins and phones stop working at once. Owners only, and not an owner.

get.description: The workspace's projects, by key: each one's key, name, and when it was created.

post.description: Creates a project: one product, with the components that ship separately. Its key is permanent. Owners only.

get.description: One project and its components, by key.

post.description: Adds a component to a project and returns its ingest key, which its telemetry is sent with. The key is shown only in this answer.

put.description: Replaces the project's settings: `productionEnvironments`, the 1 to 20 environments it calls production, where its incidents alert and its views start. Telemetry without an environment counts as production, so no alert is lost. Until a project chooses, prod, production and live.

Replaces a component's links: `repository`, its GitHub repository as owner/name, whose commits its releases are; and `deployTargets`, where its releases go in each environment: the GitHub Actions workflow that builds and deploys a release there, started with the inputs `release`, `environment`, `commit` and `runner`, and, for an app, the App Store Connect app its builds go to, for TestFlight only or through to the App Store; and `shipsWith`, another of the project's components whose deploys deploy this one too, from the same commit with the same release, for a part such as a background service. One left out is unlinked. 404 for a component the project lacks, or one it ships with that the project lacks or that is itself. Returns the component.

post.description: Issues a new SDK key for a component: the key its app's builds carry, in the app's SDK configuration, so the SDK can send the component's signals and read its manifest. It is public, as anything shipped in an app is, and grants nothing else. The component's other keys stay active until revoked, so a new build can carry the new key while older builds keep working. Listed again with sdkKeys. 404 for a project or a component that doesn't exist.

get.description: A component's SDK keys, newest first, revoked ones too: each key, when it was issued, and `revokedAt` once it is revoked. Active keys are those without `revokedAt`. 404 for a project or a component that doesn't exist.

post.description: Revokes one of a component's SDK keys: builds that carry it are refused from then on, so issue its replacement and ship it first. Revoking a key revoked before changes nothing and returns it. 404 for a project that doesn't exist, or a key that isn't one of the component's. Returns the key, with `revokedAt`.

get.description: Every operation in a period, the most counted first, or one with `operation`: how many times it ran, how many failed, and their average, p50, p80, p95 and p99 durations. Counted by the minute for periods of two days or less (kept 14 days), by the hour beyond (kept 15 months); `covered` says which part of the period the counts cover. `lastSeen` says when they last ran, whatever the period, in any environment and release, so a period without them can say when that was.

The load over a period: how many operations ran and failed, one point per step that had any, with their p50, p80, p95 and p99 durations, on a project's services, or on one operation with `operation`. A step without a point had nothing reported. Past two days the counts are hourly, so a finer step becomes an hour; `step` says which was used.

Traces worth opening in a period, or one operation's with `operation`: the slowest, slowest first, and the failed, newest first, at most 20 of each, each with its ID, which opens it with the traces endpoint. Of each operation, environment and hour, the five slowest traces and the five slowest failed ones are kept, 14 days; `covered` says which part of the period that covers.
The errors of a period, most frequent first: each error log grouped by its exception's type and stack, or by its logger and message, with when it was first and last seen. Kept 90 days.

One error, found whatever the period: what it is, when it was first and last seen, how often it happened in the period, and its latest occurrences there, with their messages, stack traces, and trace IDs: where an investigation starts. Each occurrence's ID opens it with the log line endpoint, and its trace ID and time its trace with the traces endpoint.
One warning or error by its ID, whenever it happened: an occurrence of an error or a line of the logs, with its message, exception, stack, trace ID, and attributes. Kept 90 days.

Warnings and errors, newest first, 100 at a time: filtered by level, text, logger, trace, error, or log message. Kept 90 days. Records below warning are in the archive, which the traces endpoint reads for one trace.

The log messages of a period, those with the most lines first, at most 100: warnings and errors that are the same message (one logger and template, or the same text but for its values), each with how many of its lines are at `level` and have `search` in them, and when it was first and last seen. Each message's ID opens it with the log message endpoint, and its lines with the logs endpoint's `message`. Kept 90 days; a message 15 months after it was last seen.

One log message, found whatever the period: what it is, when it was first and last seen, how many of its lines the period holds, and the errors those lines are occurrences of. Its lines are the logs endpoint's, with `message`.

Warnings and errors counted over time: a series for each level, component, or error group (`by`), at `level` or above (warn when absent), with a point for each step that had any. By error group, the 100 most frequent. Kept 90 days; `covered` says which part of the period the counts cover.

One trace across services, from the archive, found by its ID: its spans as a tree, with their durations and attributes, and its logs at every level. `around`, the time it happened, is optional: of a trace with more archive files than are read, those nearest to it are read first. Kept 90 days.

The project's open incidents, newest first, and up to 50 resolved in the last 7 days. Detectors look every minute: a monitor down two checks in a row, an operation failing at least 2% and three times its usual over 15 minutes, and a scheduled operation that missed twice its usual gap. `checkedAt` says when they last looked.

post.description: Marks an incident as being looked at, which stops its notifications, and returns it. Acknowledging it again keeps the first time.

get.description: The project's monitors, oldest first, each with its last check: the URLs fetched every minute, which pass with a status below 400 within 10 seconds.

post.description: Adds a monitor: a URL of one component, such as its health endpoint, fetched every minute from the next check on. A project has at most 20.

delete.description: Removes a monitor, and resolves its open incident, if any.

post.description: Pairs a phone with a code from a pairing link, and answers with its key, shown only this once: the phone calls the API with it as its bearer token, acting for whoever started the pairing, and sends `User-Agent: Cluenori/<app version> iOS/<iOS version>` so the deployment keeps its versions. A code that is wrong, used, or expired answers 403.

get.description: The phones paired with the deployment, the latest paired first, each with its model, iOS and app versions, and when, from which address and country, it last called.

post.description: Pairs a phone with a passkey answering /sign-in/passkey/options, acting for its member, and answers with its key, shown only this once, as pairing with a code does. The phone's passkey request names this site, which must list the app in /.well-known/apple-app-site-association. A passkey the deployment doesn't know, or an answer that doesn't hold, answers 401.

Starts pairing a phone for whoever calls: the link a phone opens to pair, shown as a QR code, `cluenori://pair?url=<deployment>&code=<pairing code>`, good once for 10 minutes. At most 5 are good at once; another drops the oldest.

delete.description: Removes a phone: its key stops working at once.

put.description: Keeps the push token of the phone whose key is the bearer token, and the APNs environment it belongs to, in place of any before: the phone calls it each time iOS gives the app a token. Any other credential, or a removed phone's key, answers 401.

post.description: Rings a phone with a test alarm, as a project that is down would, and answers 204 once APNs took it. 409 when push isn't set up or the phone has no push token yet; 502 with Apple's reason when APNs refused it, such as for a wrong key; 503 when APNs didn't answer.

get.description: What needs attention now across every project, the most urgent first: open incidents not acknowledged, errors happening now (seen in the last 15 minutes), acknowledged incidents, new errors (first seen in the last day), operations whose p95 over the last day is at least 1.5 times and 100 ms more than over the 7 days before, promotions that need a member (approved in App Store review and waiting to be released, waiting for someone to approve their environment on GitHub, or ended without their release getting there, as failed, rejected in App Store review, or lost, until a release reaches that environment), and projects with components that sent nothing in the last day; all in the environments each project calls production. Each item has its evidence and its project; `projects` names every project asked; `pulses` says how each project that answered is going, in its production environments: its load by the hour over the current hour and the 23 before it (an hour not listed had nothing reported), and its apps' people on the latest whole UTC day and the same day a week before (absent until its apps sent anything). A project that didn't answer is in `unanswered`, its items and pulse missing.

The feeds the caller sees, by name: each with the sources of the projects they see, how many entries arrived in the last 24 hours and 7 days, the last 7 days' by project, and when the newest arrived. A feed whose projects the caller sees none of isn't listed.

post.description: Makes a feed, for an owner: its name, its alert level (none, quiet, timeSensitive), and 1 to 50 sources, each a project and the event its apps track there, such as `user.registered`. From then on, each such event a project's app sends in production becomes an entry. A source in a project the deployment doesn't have answers 404; anyone but an owner, 403.

get.description: One feed's entries of the projects the caller sees, newest first, 100 at a time; `before` continues from an earlier answer's `next`. Each entry is one event a project's app tracked in production: the project, the event, when, the component, environment and release, the country, and the app's own user ID when the app identified the person. Kept 90 days.

put.description: Changes a feed, for an owner: its name, level and sources, in place of those before. Its entries stay. Saving the same again is safe. A source in a project the deployment doesn't have answers 404; anyone but an owner, 403.

delete.description: Deletes a feed and its entries, for an owner; the events stay in the projects' analytics. Anyone else answers 403.

get.description: Whether Cluenori is connected to GitHub: its GitHub App, absent until an owner connects it, and the accounts it is installed on, read from GitHub now; `problem` says why they couldn't be. Owners only.

delete.description: Disconnects GitHub: Cluenori forgets its app, and stops reading and promoting through it. The app stays on GitHub until its owner deletes it there. Owners only.

post.description: Starts connecting GitHub: the form the owner's browser posts to `action`, with the field `manifest`, so GitHub creates Cluenori's app in `organization` or their own account. It may read code and pull requests, and start workflows, where it is installed. GitHub then sends the browser back to `/api/github/connected`, which finishes, good once within an hour. Owners only; 409 while an app is connected.

get.description: The releases whose operations ran in a period, the latest first seen first, at most 30: each component's versions as it reports them in `service.version`, from the first minute each ran to the last, with a verdict against the release before it of the same component and environment. Worse when an operation got slower (a p95 at least 1.5 times and 100 ms more) or fails more (at least 5 failures, 2%, and three times the rate before), or an error was first seen in it; too early until it ran an hour and an operation ran 100 times in both. Operations are counted by release from October 2026.

One release, whatever any period, compared with the one before it, in `environment`, or without it the environment it last ran in: its whole life (`life`), a point for each 5 minutes while it ran under 6 hours, each hour under 3 days, else each UTC day, with its requests, failures and p95, its warnings and errors, and its app's people by day, each absent when nothing of it was sent, never 0, and its totals beside the release before's; the operations that got slower, fail more, got faster, or fail less, each the biggest change first; the operations new in it; the errors it logged, the most frequent first, at most 20, those first seen in it with it as `firstRelease`; the incidents that opened while it ran, of those the project keeps; its promotions; and the environments it can be promoted to, its component's deploy workflows.

post.description: Promotes a release to an environment, for the member who asks, by its component's deploy target there: starts its workflow on the repository's default branch with the inputs `release`, `environment`, `commit` (when known) and `runner` (`auto` unless given), as the workspace's GitHub App; and, when the target has an App Store Connect app, follows its build there once processed: for TestFlight, sets What to Test from the release's notes; for the App Store, submits it for review with its notes as What's New, as `submission` says (as soon as approved, phased, unless given). Cluenori follows it each minute until it ends, and records who started it and why. 409 while the component's last promotion to that environment hasn't ended; 422 when it can't start until someone fixes what `reason` says, where `fix` says; 503 when GitHub didn't answer. Each call that succeeds starts a run.

Promotes a commit that has no release yet, such as an app's newest: `commit`, or the newest on its repository's default branch, which GitHub is asked for. Cluenori numbers it as the component's next release, as its CI would (a commit numbered before is that release again), then promotes that release as the promote route does, with the same answers. 422 with `fix: version` until the component's version is set.

Releases a promotion that App Store review approved and that waits for a member, submitted to be released manually: App Store Connect makes it live, and the promotion ends once it is. 404 for no promotion of that ID waiting so.

get.description: How each component's releases reach its environments: the environments of its deploy targets, in their order (for a component without any, those it ran in), each with the release there now and since when, a promotion to it that hasn't ended, and what can go there next: `promote` the release of the environment before it, newer than the one there, or, to the first, `buildLatest`, the default branch's newest commit. An App Store app's environment has the build out on the App Store; a TestFlight app's, the latest build processed; another, the release last deployed or first run there.

Each component's version, `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`, which its next builds are numbered in, and the last build number given: a commit built for the first time becomes `<version>+<last + 1>`, for good. A component whose version was never set isn't listed; its CI can't number builds until it is.

put.description: Sets a component's version, such as a bump of its patch, minor or major: the same or higher than now. Its build numbers continue, or from `firstBuild`, above the last given. 422 for a lower version, a first build at or below the last, or a component the project lacks.
Replaces a release's notes for its users, one for each language, up to 4000 characters each: its What's New when it goes to the App Store, and What to Test in TestFlight.

post.description: Drafts a release's notes for where it goes: written by the project's language model from the commits since the release current in `environment` (on the App Store, the live one), in the project's notes style, with its last notes as examples; one for each language of the app the environment's builds go to, or English. Saves nothing: edit the draft and save it. 503 when its commits aren't known, or GitHub or the model don't answer.

get.description: How the project's release notes read, in its own words, which drafts follow: the project's, or Cluenori's default until it sets one.

put.description: Sets how the project's release notes read, up to 2000 characters.

get.description: Each app component's version policy: releases below `minimum` must update before they can be used, those below `recommended` are offered it in a sheet people can close; with the store page to update from, the oldest OS the update runs on, and the project's words for each decision by language. It applies in the project's production environments, to releases whose version (the part before `+`) is one to four numbers, compared part by part. A component without a policy isn't listed; its releases are never asked to update. Apps read it in their manifest within five minutes.

put.description: Replaces a component's version policy: what is left out is unset, so send every field to keep. `minimum`, `recommended`, or both, the recommended not lower; at most 40 `words`, one for each language and decision (`require` or `recommend`), which the app shows instead of its own. Without `storeUrl`, the App Store page of the app its App Store deploy target names (one in production first) is asked of App Store Connect. 422 for a component the project lacks, neither version, a recommended version lower than the minimum, or no store URL given or found.

delete.description: Removes a component's version policy: its releases are no longer asked to update, once apps read their manifest again, within five minutes. Removing one that isn't set does nothing.

get.description: How a project's apps were used in a period, by UTC day: the people active (DAU), the people of the 7 and the 30 days ending each day (WAU and MAU), installations, sessions (each time the app came to the foreground) and their foreground time; over the whole period, people, installations, sessions per person and per person and day, and each release's people. Only what the apps' SDKs sent counts: days before the first batch, or older than the 15 months kept, aren't listed, and a week or month that reaches before them has no count, never zero. Narrow it by component, environment and release.

Weekly cohorts of the people first seen in a period, by the UTC week (Monday to Sunday) each was first seen in a component and environment: how many there were, and how many were active in each week since, the first being all of them and the last the week now is in, so far. Activity is kept 15 months.

The app health of the releases that sent anything in a period, the latest first seen first, at most 30, each over all that is kept of it and beside the release before it of the same component and environment: sessions and people; launch times to the first frame and to the first useful screen, p50 and p95, cold and warm, prewarmed launches only counted; peak memory and footprint p95; MetricKit's crashes and hangs, and per 1,000 sessions. Worse when a launch kind's p95 is at least 1.5 times and 100 ms more than before (both with 50 launches), peak memory's p95 1.25 times and 50 MB more (50 measurements), or crashes or hangs at least 5, twice the rate and 2 per 1,000 sessions more (both with 200 sessions and MetricKit's reports); too early until it ran an hour and a measure compares. What a release didn't send is absent, not zero.

How each feature key was used in a period, the most people first: the people who did anything in it, its events and screens, and the app's memory there (peak and footprint p95); signals the app marked with no feature are the row without a key, "(no feature)", whose share says how much is tagged.

One person of the project, by the ID Cluenori gave them: the app's user IDs linked to them, when they were first and last seen, their installations (component, release, device, country), the days they were active with their sessions, the latest 90, the features they used over 15 months with their days, events and screens, the last used first, at most 50, and their timeline: the latest 1,000 sessions, launches, screens, events and MetricKit reports, newest first.
The person the app's own user ID `user` is linked to, as the person route answers: what did this user do. 404 when the apps never sent it.

One feature's story, by its key exactly, over everything kept of it, with no period, in one environment or every one: how the apps used it, each UTC day's people, events and screens (15 months), everyone who used it, the 20 who used it last, its releases and the app's memory in it; and what its services sent naming it in `cluenori.feature`: each UTC day's warnings and errors and its 10 most frequent errors (90 days), and each day's operations by component and operation, with how many failed (15 months). A part nothing named the feature in is empty; 404 when nothing kept names it.
